text:
jordan: Heads-up — I sketched a small proposal: a "metering shim" HTTP push interface runtime teams can call to emit lightweight billing events. Idea is to keep the runtime integration tiny and move complexity into the metering pipeline. :eyes:

sasha: brief explainer pls — what does 'lightweight' mean in fields/size and guarantees?

jordan: Minimal required fields: tenant_id, request_id, model_id, token_counts (prompt|completion), event_ts, provenance_id (optional), and a signature for auth. No full trace blobs. Think < 1KB per event.

kevin: how do we handle retries / idempotency? If runtimes crash and replay, we can't double-bill.

jordan: plan: require an idempotency_key (UUID) and an event_seq for chunked requests. Server-side will dedupe using (tenant_id, idempotency_key). Also accept a tombstone event for revoke cases.

maria: what about attribution for multi-model pipelines (e.g., reranker -> generator)? We need per-step attribution so charge split is possible.

jordan: shim supports an optional "stages" array. Each stage = {name, model_id, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, processed_ms}. We'll include a canonical "primary_model" field for pricing default.

sasha: schema sample?

jordan: ```json
{
  "tenant_id": "acct_ABC123",
  "request_id": "r-0001",
  "idempotency_key": "c4a1f6f0-...",
  "event_ts": "2026-03-15T18:42:12Z",
  "primary_model": "redwood/gptx-1.2b",
  "token_counts": {"prompt": 45, "completion": 128},
  "stages": [
    {"name":"rerank","model_id":"open/rank-200","tokens_prompt":10,"tokens_completion":0},
    {"name":"gen","model_id":"redwood/gptx-1.2b","tokens_prompt":35,"tokens_completion":128}
  ],
  "provenance_id": "prov-9f2",
  "signature": "v1:..."
}
```

kevin: good. How do we keep privacy? provenance_id must not leak PII.

maria: require provenance to be an opaque token (no payload) and force KMS-wrapped values if customers opt-in to richer trace. Default: provenance_id is synthetic fingerprint only.

sasha: late-arrival handling? We already have late tokens flows in ledger.

jordan: shim accepts late events with a "event_origin_ts" and an "ingest_ts" added server-side. We'll apply a late-arrival window (configurable per-tenant) and mark events outside window as "late" for downstream reconciliation. Also emit a routing hint so they go to the audit lane.

ops-bot: NOTE: Audit lane will store raw events for 90 days by default. Reconcile jobs run hourly.

kevin: sampling for high-throughput customers? Can't ship every tiny op.

jordan: support sampled mode — shim can mark event.sample_rate (e.g., 0.01) and include full-scale multiplier to reconstruct expected counts. But sampled events must be deterministic (hash of request_id % 1/sample_rate) to avoid bias.

maria: rollout plan? Need e2e tests + fallbacks before we flip runtime integrations.

jordan: proposal: 1) land schema + server stub, 2) pilot with internal runtimes on feature-flagged tenants, 3) enable sampled mode for a few heavy tenants, 4) full opt-in across dedicated fleet, 5) deprecate older sidecar shim in 3 months.

sasha: ops concerns: monitoring for mismatch between shim counts and legacy path. We need diffs + alerting.

jordan: agree — add per-tenant daily reconciliation job that reports token_delta_pct and spikes. Alert if > 2% for > 6 hours. Also surface per-model anomalies in Console.

kevin: TODOs for eng-platform: add schema registry entry, dedupe store design, sampling flag in runtime SDK, reconciliation dashboard.

maria: I'll write an ops runbook for late arrivals and revoke/tombstone flows.

jordan: thanks all. If nobody objects I'll open an RFC follow-up with schema + migration steps tomorrow. :+1:
